module_title: South Indian Marvels and the Sultanate Era
introduction: South Indian temples are famous for their 'Gopurams' and Dravidian style. This level focuses on the Chola and Pallava dynasties, along with key Sultanate structures.

core_concepts.title: Brihadeeswarar Temple
core_concepts.description:
Location: Thanjavur, **Tamil Nadu**. 
Builder: **Rajaraja Chola I**. 
Key Feature: Dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is the world's first temple built entirely of **Granite**. It is also called the 'Rajarajeshwaram Temple'.

core_concepts.title: Meenakshi Amman Temple
core_concepts.description:
Location: Madurai, **Tamil Nadu**. 
Builder: Primarily the Pandya and Nayaka dynasties. 
Key Feature: Situated on the banks of the Vaigai River. It is famous for its 14 magnificent 'Gopurams' (gateway towers).

core_concepts.title: Qutub Minar
core_concepts.description:
Location: New Delhi. 
Construction: Started by **Qutub-ud-din Aibak**, three more storeys added by **Iltutmish**, and the 5th/final storey repaired/completed by **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**.

core_concepts.title: Fatehpur Sikri
core_concepts.description:
Location: Near Agra, UP. 
Builder: **Akbar**. 
Key Feature: Akbar built the **Buland Darwaza** (highest gateway in India) here to commemorate his victory over Gujarat.

important_entities.name: Dravidian Architecture
important_entities.significance: Unlike Northern temples (Nagara), Southern temples (Dravida) are characterized by pyramid-shaped towers called 'Vimana' and massive, ornate entrance gateways called 'Gopurams'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If the question asks 'Who completed the construction?', the answer is **Iltutmish**. If it asks 'Who started it?', the answer is **Aibak**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The Brihadeeswarar temple (Brihad means big) was built by Rajaraja Chola I.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent UPSC/State PCS question: 'The Brihadeeswarar temple at Thanjavur is a masterpiece of which dynasty?' Answer: Chola Dynasty.
